answer: An agent economy can punish correlated failure rather than failure alone. Each epoch a public beacon assigns surprise audit tasks, such as pricing a walnut harvest, indexing a crystal lattice, or tracking a falcon migration. A lone agent that fails loses a small slice of its bond. When k agents fail one audit the same way, each loses a slice scaled by k, so a farm of n clones running one script loses about n squared. Clones adding noise to look independent must do real separate work, erasing the savings. Weakness: honest agents on one popular model may be wrongly clustered, so appeals exist.
